This resolves the anaphor at 35:22a: 'While Israel lived in that land' (בָּאָרֶץ הַהִוא) refers back to Migdal Eder, named in 35:21. Verse 35:22 remains bipartite and is retained whole under the whole-verse span constraint: the Masoretic mid-verse break, a petuchah functioning as piska be'emtsa pasuq (single-witness, retagged consistently with the 35:29 marker below), separates Reuben's sin (22a, narrative continuation of 35:21) from the list header 'Now the sons of Jacob were twelve' (22b), which is itself a boundary-driving list-register formula launching the four-member Leah/Rachel/Bilhah/Zilpah series (23-26) and bound by inclusio to 35:26's closing 'these are the sons of Jacob'. This internal 22a|22b seam -- narrative giving way to register, reinforced by the coinciding mid-verse petuchah and the verse's own atnach -- is a real sub-unit division; it is not enacted as a chunk edge only because the whole-verse constraint forbids splitting 22a from 22b, not because no seam exists there. The span is accordingly composite rather than a pure list: itinerary/narrative (21-22a), register list (22b-26), and a death-and-burial report (27-29) -- outnumbering the list in verse count -- closing on Isaac's death formula (35:27-29), corroborated by a petuchah after 35:29 (single-witness) before the fresh toledot at 36:1.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Starting at 35:22, leaving 35:21 with the preceding unit -- withdrawn because it separated the נסע construction's two instances inconsistently and left 35:22a's locative anaphor without its antecedent. A second, distinct alternative -- splitting at 35:22a|22b, where the register formula actually begins -- is acknowledged as a real seam rather than a null option: it is suppressed only by the whole-verse span constraint (Reuben's sin and the list header cannot be separated at the verse level), not by any absence of textual signal.

boundary_rationale: Opens on Joseph's secret instruction to plant the cup (44:1-2); the start verse has a zero subject inheriting its referent from 43:34 (Joseph is not named again until 44:2b), which is syntactic continuity across the chapter break, not an independent Hebrew onset, and the record now says so plainly. The start is chosen on discourse-frame grounds instead: the cup-planting stratagem's commissioning speech opens the test sequence, and keeping it with its own execution (the overtaking, the discovery) outweighs the stronger clause-level markers nearby -- the asyndetic verbless 44:3 (הַבֹּקֶר אוֹר, WEB's subordinating 'As soon as the morning was light') and the fronted 44:4 (הֵם יָצְאוּ, WEB's 'When they had gone out of the city') -- both logged as competing internal onsets that WEB's subordinating renderings obscure. Closes on Joseph's initial verdict before Judah's plea begins (44:17).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Starting at 44:3 or 44:4, both more strongly marked in Hebrew than 44:1 -- preserved as competing onsets, not adopted because the secret instruction (44:1-2) is the discourse-frame's true beginning: the stratagem's commission belongs with its own execution.

boundary_rationale: Opens on a new occasion notice, "After these things, someone said to Joseph, Behold, your father is sick" (48:1); Joseph brings Manasseh and Ephraim with him in this same verse, and Jacob's sustained first-person speech (48:3-7) both recounts the Luz theophany and Rachel's death AND formally names and adopts the two sons already present (48:5-6), so the sons' absence is not, and cannot be, the ground for the 48:7/48:8 division. The real division is discourse mode: Jacob's first-person speech, including the fronted וַאֲנִי at 48:7, gives way to wayyiqtol narration at 48:8 ('Israel saw Joseph's sons, and said, Who are these?'), which restarts the scene's action as if seeing them for the first time.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Claiming the sons are not yet brought forward as the ground for this division -- withdrawn, directly contradicted by 48:1b and 48:5-6 within this same span; the real ground is the discourse-mode shift from sustained first-person speech to narrated action.

boundary_rationale: Opens on verse 49:28, which the Masoretic athnach divides into an enumerative colophon closing the preceding poem (28a, 'All these are the twelve tribes of Israel...he blessed everyone according to his own blessing' -- in form, a closing summary belonging with M8-Gen-114's material) and the prose resumption this decision is actually about (28b, 'and this is what their father spoke to them, and blessed them', itself already a summary transitioning into the burial instructions). Verse-level tiling cannot split 28a from 28b, so the whole verse is retained here, with 28a's residue recorded rather than left implicit. Runs through Jacob's burial instructions, closing on his death (49:33).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Describing 49:28 as if it were straightforwardly this chunk's own 'opening' evidence without noting its bipartite, colophon-then-resumption character -- withdrawn as imprecise; the corrected description above is more accurate about what the verse actually contains.
